english: You will go on Liburnian galleys among the high, of ships,
note: Liburnis (sc. navibus): light, fast Liburnian galleys; alta agrees with propugnacula (line 2).

english: friend, bulwarks,
note: propugnacula: the towering decks of the great warships (Antony's fleet), literally 'bulwarks'.

english: ready every danger of Caesar
note: omne ... periculum: every danger of Caesar, i.e. that threatens Caesar (Octavian).

english: to undergo, Maecenas, at your own [risk]:
note: tuo agrees with periculo understood: 'at your own peril'.

latin: quid nos, quibus te vita sit superstite
english: what [shall] we [do], for whom, with you surviving, life may be
note: quid nos: the verb is omitted. te ... superstite: ablative absolute, 'if you live'; sit is subjunctive (generic/causal relative).

english: pleasant, if otherwise, burdensome?
note: si contra: 'if the contrary' (if you do not survive); gravis agrees with vita (line 5).

english: Shall we, as bidden, pursue leisure,
note: utrumne ... an (line 9): 'whether ... or'; iussi: 'having been ordered' (by Maecenas).

english: not sweet unless together with you,
note: dulce agrees with otium (line 7).

latin: an hunc laborem mente laturi, decet
english: or this toil, ready to bear [it] with a mind, [such as] it befits
note: laturi: future participle, 'ready to bear'; mente qua (line 10): 'with that spirit with which'.

english: with which to bear [it] men not soft?
note: qua refers to mente (line 9); non mollis (= molles) viros: men who are not soft, i.e. brave men, subject of ferre with decet.

latin: feremus et te vel per Alpium iuga
english: We will bear [it], and you either through the Alps' ridges
and the inhospitable Caucasus
note: inhospitalem agrees with Caucasum.

latin: vel occidentis usque ad ultimum sinum
english: or of the west right up to the farthest bay
note: occidentis ... sinum: the farthest gulf of the West.

english: we will follow with brave breast.
note: pectore: 'heart', courage.

latin: roges, tuom labore quid iuvem meo,
english: You might ask how I might help your toil with my own,
note: roges: potential subjunctive; iuvem: subjunctive in indirect question; tuom (archaic for tuum) agrees with laborem understood from labore, 'your labour with my labour'.

english: unwarlike and firm too little?
note: parum: 'not enough'.

latin: comes minore sum futurus in metu,
english: As a companion I shall be in less fear,
note: sum futurus: periphrastic future, 'I am going to be'.

english: which [fear] holds the absent in greater [measure]:
note: qui (sc. metus) maior: the fear which grips the absent more; absentis = absentes.

english: as a bird sitting by its featherless chicks
note: its supplied.

english: the serpents' gliding-up fears
note: adlapsus: the stealthy approach.

latin: magis relictis, non, ut adsit, auxili
english: more for them left, not, though she should be present, of help
note: relictis (sc. pullis): when they are left; ut adsit: concessive, 'even if she were there'; auxili (genitive) goes with plus (line 22).

english: about to bring more to them present.
note: latura: future participle, 'being likely to bring'; praesentibus (sc. pullis): to the chicks if she were with them.

english: Willingly this and every will be soldiered,
note: militabitur: impersonal passive future, 'this ... will be campaigned'; omne agrees with bellum (line 24).

english: war, in hope of your favour,
note: tuae ... gratiae: of your good will.

english: not so that to more bullocks yoked
note: inligata agrees with aratra (line 26).

english: ploughs may strain of mine
note: nitantur: subjunctive of purpose; meis agrees with iuvencis (line 25): 'so that my ploughs may labour yoked to more bullocks'.

english: or so that my herd, for Calabrian before the Star burning
note: pecusve ... mutet: 'or that my flock may exchange'; my supplied; Calabris agrees with pascuis (line 28); Sidus fervidum: the Dog Star, at midsummer (capital S as in the source).

english: Lucanian [pastures] may exchange, pastures,
note: Lucana (sc. pascua) is the object of mutet; pascuis (ablative) completes Calabris (line 27): flocks driven between winter pastures in Calabria and summer pastures in Lucania.

latin: neque ut superni villa candens Tusculi
english: nor so that a villa, shining, of lofty Tusculum,
note: superni agrees with Tusculi; villa candens: a white marble villa.

english: may touch the Circaean walls:
note: Circaea moenia: Tusculum, said to be founded by Telegonus, son of Circe.

english: enough and more me your kindness
has enriched; not at all shall I have acquired
note: haud paravero: future perfect, 'I shall not have acquired' (i.e. I will not seek wealth).

latin: quod aut avarus ut Chremes terra premam,
english: [anything] which either, a miser like Chremes, I may hide in earth,
note: premam: subjunctive (relative of purpose); Chremes: the miser of comedy.

english: or, an ungirt spendthrift, I may squander.
note: discinctus: 'ungirt', loose-living; nepos: literally 'grandson', a spendthrift heir; perdam: subjunctive.

english: “Happy that man who far from business,
note: Quotation mark as in the source: Alfius' speech runs to line 66. negotiis: business, especially money-lending.

english: like the ancient race of mortals,
ancestral fields with oxen works his own,
note: suis agrees with bubus: 'with his own oxen'.

english: freed from every interest-debt
note: faenore: interest, debt.

english: and is not roused by the trumpet, a soldier, savage,
note: truci agrees with classico.

english: and does not shudder at the angry sea
and avoids the forum and the proud of citizens
note: superba agrees with limina (line 8).

english: more powerful thresholds.
note: potentiorum agrees with civium (line 7): the doorways of great men, where clients wait.

english: Therefore either with the grown, of vines, layering
note: adulta agrees with propagine: the grown layering of vines

english: the tall he weds poplars
note: maritat: 'marries' the vines to poplars; metaphor for training vines on trees.

english: or in a withdrawn valley of lowing [cattle]
note: mugientium (sc. boum).

english: he gazes out at the wandering herds
note: errantis = errantes.

english: and, useless with the pruning-hook branches cutting off,
note: inutilis (= inutiles) agrees with ramos.

english: more fruitful ones he grafts in
note: feliciores (sc. ramos).

latin: aut pressa puris mella condit amphoris
english: or pressed honey he stores in clean jars
note: pressa mella: honey squeezed from the comb.

english: or shears the weak sheep.
note: ovis = oves.

latin: vel cum decorum mitibus pomis caput
english: Or when, adorned with mellow fruits, his head
note: decorum agrees with caput; his supplied.

english: Autumn from the fields has raised,
how he rejoices, grafted plucking pears
note: insitiva agrees with pira: pears from grafted trees.

english: and the grape rivalling purple,

latin: qua muneretur te, Priape, et te, pater
english: with which he may reward you, Priapus, and you, father
note: muneretur: subjunctive (relative of purpose).

english: Silvanus, guardian of boundaries.

latin: libet iacere modo sub antiqua ilice,
english: It is pleasing to lie now under an ancient holm-oak,
note: libet: 'it pleases [him]'.

english: now in the clinging grass:
note: tenaci: thick, matted.

english: there glide meanwhile between high banks the waters,
note: altis ... ripis: 'within deep banks'.

english: complain in the woods the birds
note: queruntur: 'lament', of birdsong. Silvis capitalised as in the source.

english: and the leaves to the springs murmur against, flowing,
note: manantibus agrees with lymphis; some texts read fontes for frondes.

english: [a thing] which may invite light sleep.
note: quod: 'which', i.e. the sound; invitet: subjunctive; levis (= leves) agrees with somnos.

latin: at cum tonantis annus hibernus Iovis
english: But when of thundering the year wintry, of Jove,
note: tonantis agrees with Iovis; annus hibernus: the winter season.

english: rains and snows brings together,
note: imbris = imbres; conparat: gathers.

latin: aut trudit acris hinc et hinc multa cane
english: either he drives fierce, from here and there, with many a dog,
note: acris (= acres) agrees with apros (line 32); multa cane: collective singular.

english: boars into the obstructing nets
note: plagas: hunting nets; obstantis = obstantes.

latin: aut amite levi rara tendit retia
english: or on a smooth pole wide-meshed spreads nets,
note: amite: the fowler's forked pole.

english: for greedy thrushes snares,
note: dolos: 'tricks', in apposition to retia.

latin: pavidumque leporem et advenam laqueo gruem
english: and the timid hare and the migrant with a noose, the crane,
note: advenam agrees with gruem.

english: pleasant prizes, he catches.
note: praemia in apposition to leporem and gruem.

latin: quis non malarum quas amor curas habet
english: Who does not of the evil cares which love has
note: malarum agrees with curarum, attracted into the relative clause as curas.

english: among these things forget?

latin: quodsi pudica mulier in partem iuvet
english: But if a chaste wife for her part should help
note: iuvet: subjunctive (future less vivid condition); in partem: 'in her share'.

english: the house and sweet children,
note: dulcis = dulces.

english: such as a Sabine or one scorched by the suns,
note: Solibus: capital S as in the source.

english: wife of a swift Apulian,
should pile up a sacred of old logs hearth
note: exstruat: subjunctive; sacrum agrees with focum; vetustis ... lignis: seasoned wood.

english: before the coming of her weary husband
note: lassi agrees with viri; sub adventum: 'near the time of the arrival'; her supplied. Sub capitalised as in the source.

english: and, shutting in woven hurdles the glad flock,
note: textis cratibus: wattled pens.

english: should drain their distended udders
note: siccet: subjunctive (milk them dry); their supplied.

latin: et horna dulci vina promens dolio
english: and this year's from the sweet wine bringing out jar
note: horna agrees with vina; dulci agrees with dolio.

english: should prepare unbought feasts:
note: adparet: subjunctive; inemptas: home-grown.

english: not me would Lucrine please shellfish
note: iuverint: perfect subjunctive (or future perfect) in the apodosis; Lucrine: from the Lucrine lake, famed for oysters.

english: or more a turbot or parrot-fish,
note: scari: a prized fish.

english: if any, having thundered on the eastern waves,
note: intonata: perfect participle

english: a storm to this sea should turn,
note: vertat: subjunctive; hoc mare: the Italian sea.

latin: non Afra avis descendat in ventrem meum,
english: not would an African bird descend into my belly,
note: descendat: subjunctive; Afra avis: guinea-fowl.

english: not an Ionian francolin
note: attagen: a game bird.

english: more pleasant than, gathered from the richest
note: pinguissimis agrees with ramis (line 56).

english: olive, branches of the trees,
note: oliva: the olive picked from the branches.

latin: aut herba lapathi prata amantis et gravi
english: or the plant of sorrel, lover of meadows, and to heavy
note: lapathi: sorrel; prata amantis: 'loving the meadows'; gravi agrees with corpori (line 58).

english: mallows healthful to the body
note: salubres agrees with malvae; mallow as a mild laxative for a heavy (sluggish) body.

english: or a lamb slain at the festal Terminalia
note: Terminalia: festival of the boundary god Terminus, 23 February.

english: or a kid snatched from the wolf.

latin: has inter epulas ut iuvat pastas ovis
english: Amid these feasts how it pleases, pastured, sheep
note: pastas agrees with ovis (= oves).

english: to see hurrying home,
note: properantis = properantes, agreeing with ovis (line 61).

english: to see, weary, the ploughshare upturned, the oxen
note: fessos agrees with boves; inversum: turned upside down for the journey home.

english: dragging with neck drooping,
note: trahentis = trahentes, agreeing with boves (line 63); languido agrees with collo.

english: and the set-out home-born slaves, swarm of a rich house,
note: positos agrees with vernas: seated (at dinner); vernas: slaves born in the house; examen: 'swarm' of bees, the household's crowd.

english: around the gleaming Lares.”
note: renidentis (= renidentes) may agree with vernas (line 65), the slaves beaming, or be taken with Laris (= Lares), the shining household gods; quotation mark as in the source.

english: These things when he had spoken, the money-lender Alfius,
note: faenerator: usurer.

english: now, now about to be a countryman,
all called in on the Ides his money,
note: omnem agrees with pecuniam; idibus: the mid-month settlement day for loans.

english: seeks on the Kalends to place [it].
note: ponere: to invest (lend) again; Kalends: the first of the month.

english: A parent's, if ever anyone with impious hand
note: parentis agrees with guttur (line 2) as a genitive; inpia agrees with manu; olim: 'at any time'.

english: aged throat shall have broken,
note: fregerit: future perfect; senile agrees with guttur.

english: let him eat than hemlock garlic more harmful.
note: edit: archaic subjunctive (= edat), jussive; cicutis: ablative of comparison.

english: O hard reapers' guts.
note: ilia: the bowels; the reapers ate garlic with their food.

latin: quid hoc veneni saevit in praecordiis?
english: What of poison is this that rages in my innards?
note: quid hoc veneni: 'what poison is this?'; praecordiis: the vitals; my supplied.

english: Surely not viper's blood in these
note: num expects 'no'; viperinus agrees with cruor; his agrees with herbis (line 7).

latin: incoctus herbis me fefellit? an malas
english: cooked in herbs has deceived me? Or evil
note: incoctus agrees with cruor (line 6); malas agrees with dapes (line 8).

english: Canidia handled the feasts?
note: Canidia: the witch of Epodes 5 and 17, here imagined as cook.

english: As, beyond all the Argonauts, the shining
note: candidum agrees with ducem (line 10).

english: Medea admired the leader,
note: ut ... mirata est: 'when' or 'as' Medea admired.

english: unknown to the bulls about to bind yokes,
note: ignota agrees with iuga; inligaturum agrees with Iasonem (line 12).

english: she smeared with this Jason,
note: hoc: this (garlic), the drug she gave him.

english: with this, gifts smeared, having avenged herself on her rival,
note: delibutis donis: ablative absolute, the gifts smeared with this (the poison)

english: on a serpent she fled winged.
note: alite agrees with serpente: her winged-dragon chariot.

latin: nec tantus umquam Siderum insedit vapor
english: Nor so great ever of the stars has settled a heat
note: tantus agrees with vapor; Siderum (capital S as in the source): the Dog Star season.

english: on thirsty Apulia,
note: siticulosae Apuliae: dative with insedit.

english: nor the gift on the shoulders of effective Hercules
note: munus: the shirt of Nessus; efficacis: 'strong, accomplishing'.

english: burned more hotly.
But if anything ever such you shall have desired,
note: concupiveris: future perfect.

english: jesting Maecenas, I pray,
her hand may the girl against your kiss set,
note: opponat: subjunctive (wish); savio: a kiss; her supplied.

english: and on the far edge of the bed may she lie.
note: extrema agrees with sponda; cubet: subjunctive.

latin: Lupis et agnis quanta Sortito obtigit,
english: To wolves and lambs as great as by lot has fallen,
note: quanta (sc. discordia) ... obtigit: as great a hatred as nature allotted; Sortito capitalised as in the source.

english: with you to me hatred is,
note: discordia: 'enmity'.

english: you burned by Spanish ropes on your side
note: peruste: vocative; latus: accusative of respect; Hibericis funibus: ropes of Spanish broom used for flogging.

english: and on your legs by the hard fetter.
note: crura: accusative of respect; dura agrees with compede.

english: Although, proud through money, you may walk,
note: pecunia: ablative of cause

english: fortune does not change birth.
note: genus: class, descent.

english: Do you see, as the Sacred you measure out Way,
note: metiente te: ablative absolute; sacram agrees with viam: the Via Sacra.

english: with your of twice three ells toga,
note: bis trium ulnarum: six ells wide, an ostentatious toga; your supplied.

latin: ut ora vertat huc et huc euntium
english: how the faces it turns this way and that of those going by,
note: vertat: subjunctive in indirect question; euntium: of the passers-by.

english: the most free indignation?
note: liberrima: outspoken.

english: “Cut with the whips, this man, of the triumvirs,
note: triumviralibus agrees with flagellis: the tresviri capitales, magistrates who flogged slaves; quotation mark as in the source.

english: to the herald's disgust,
note: praeconis ad fastidium: flogged until even the crier proclaiming his crime grew weary.

english: ploughs of Falernian a thousand of estate acres
note: Falerni (sc. agri) fundi: of land in the Falernian district.

english: and the Appian with ponies wears down
note: Appiam (sc. viam); mannis: Gallic ponies, a luxury.

english: and on the benches, a great man, in the first, a knight,
note: primis agrees with sedilibus: the front fourteen rows reserved for knights.

english: Otho being scorned, sits.
note: Othone contempto: ablative absolute; the lex Roscia of L. Roscius Otho reserved those seats for knights.

latin: quid attinet tot ora navium gravi
english: What does it matter so many faces of ships with heavy
note: ora navium: the beaks; gravi agrees with pondere (line 18).

english: beaked to be led weight
note: rostrata agrees with ora (line 17).

english: against brigands and a servile band,
note: latrones ... manum: Sextus Pompeius' pirates and runaway slaves.

english: with this, this man as tribune of soldiers?”
note: hoc, hoc tribuno: ablative absolute, 'with this man as military tribune'; quotation mark as in the source.

latin: “At o deorum quidquid in caelo regit
english: “But O, of gods whatever in heaven rules
note: quidquid deorum: 'whatever gods there are'; the boy speaks (quotation mark as in the source).

english: the lands and the human race,

latin: quid iste fert tumultus aut quid omnium
english: what does that uproar mean, or why of all
note: iste ... tumultus: 'that commotion of yours'.

english: the faces upon me alone fierce?
note: voltus (= vultus) ... truces: the verb (sc. fert, 'are turned') is omitted.

latin: per liberos te, si vocata partubus
english: By your children, if, summoned to births
note: te: you (Canidia); partubus agrees with veris (line 6).

english: Lucina real attended,
note: veris: real (not feigned) births; Lucina: goddess of childbirth.

latin: per hoc inane purpurae decus precor,
english: by this empty of purple ornament I pray,
note: inane agrees with decus: his purple-bordered toga (praetexta), now useless.

english: by about to condemn these things Jupiter,
note: inprobaturum agrees with Iovem.

latin: quid ut noverca me intueris aut uti
english: why like a stepmother do you stare at me or like
note: uti = ut.

english: a beast attacked with steel?”
note: petita agrees with belua.

latin: ut haec trementi questus ore constitit
english: When these things with trembling, having complained, mouth he stood still,
note: trementi agrees with ore; questus: having complained; constitit: stood.

english: his insignia snatched off, the boy,
note: insignibus raptis: ablative absolute, the bulla and toga praetexta; his supplied.

english: a beardless body, such as could the impious
note: inpube corpus: in apposition to puer; posset: subjunctive (characteristic); inpia agrees with pectora (line 14).

english: soften, of the Thracians the hearts:
Canidia, with short entwined vipers
note: illigata agrees with Canidia; brevibus agrees with viperis.

english: as to her hair and her unkempt head,
note: crinis (= crines) and caput: accusatives of respect; her supplied.

english: orders from tombs wild fig-trees uprooted,
note: erutas agrees with caprificos; iubet ... aduri (line 24): 'orders ... to be burned'.

english: orders cypresses funereal
note: funebris = funebres, agreeing with cupressos.

latin: et uncta turpis ova ranae Sanguine
english: and smeared of a foul eggs frog with blood
note: uncta agrees with ova; turpis agrees with ranae; Sanguine capitalised as in the source.

english: and the feather of a nocturnal screech-owl
note: strigis: the strix, bird of witchcraft.

english: and herbs which Iolcos and Hiberia
note: Hiberia: in the Caucasus, near Colchis.

english: sends, fertile in poisons,
note: ferax agrees with Hiberia (line 21).

latin: et ossa ab ore rapta ieiunae canis
english: and bones from the mouth snatched of a fasting bitch
note: ieiunae canis: of a hungry dog (canis feminine).

english: to be burned with Colchian flames.
note: aduri depends on iubet (line 17); Colchian: like Medea's.

latin: at expedita Sagana, per totam domum
english: But girt-up Sagana, through the whole house
note: expedita: ready for action, skirts tucked.

english: sprinkling Avernal waters,
note: Avernalis = Avernales: from Lake Avernus, entrance to the underworld.

english: bristles with rough hair, like a sea-
note: asperis agrees with capillis; marinus agrees with echinus (line 28).

english: urchin or a Laurentine boar.
Driven off by no, Veia, conscience,
note: abacta agrees with Veia; nulla agrees with conscientia: 'deterred by no conscience'.

english: with hard mattocks the ground
was emptying, groaning at the labours,
note: exhauriebat: imperfect, 'was digging out'.

english: where could, buried, the boy
note: quo: 'so that there'; posset: subjunctive (purpose).

latin: longo die bis terque mutatae dapis
english: through the long day, twice and three times changed, of a meal
note: mutatae agrees with dapis; longo die: ablative of duration.

english: die-away at the spectacle,
note: inemori: 'die in', 'pine away at'; spectaculo goes with dapis (line 33): 'at the sight of food changed two or three times'.

latin: cum promineret ore, quantum exstant aqua
english: when he would jut out with his face as much as stand out of water
note: promineret: subjunctive; quantum exstant: 'as far as ... project'; his supplied.

english: suspended by the chin bodies;
note: suspensa agrees with corpora: swimmers' bodies held up to the chin.

latin: exsucta uti medulla et aridum iecur
english: so that, sucked out, the marrow and the dry liver
note: uti = ut (purpose); exsucta agrees with medulla.

english: of love should be a cup,
note: esset: subjunctive; amoris poculum: a love potion.

english: when, on forbidden once fixed food,
note: interminato agrees with cibo: food forbidden to him; fixae agrees with pupulae (line 40).

english: should have wasted away his eyes.
note: intabuissent: pluperfect subjunctive; pupulae: the pupils, eyes; his supplied.

english: Not to have been lacking in masculine lust
note: masculae libidinis: a woman's lust for women, 'mannish lust'; the genitive goes with defuisse.

english: Ariminian Folia
note: Folia of Ariminum (Rimini), a witch; accusative subject of defuisse.

english: both idle believed Neapolis
note: otiosa agrees with Neapolis: Naples, town of leisure and gossip.

english: and every neighbouring town,
[she] who stars charmed down with a voice Thessalian
note: quae: Folia (line 42); excantata agrees with sidera; Thessala agrees with voce: Thessaly was the land of witches.

english: and the moon from the sky drags down.
Here an uncut savage with tooth livid
note: inresectum agrees with pollicem (line 48); saeva agrees with Canidia (line 48); livido agrees with dente.

english: Canidia gnawing thumb
note: her thumb (thumbnail) uncut; pollicem completes inresectum (line 47).

latin: quid dixit aut quid tacuit? “o rebus meis
english: what did she say, or what not say? “O to my affairs
note: quid tacuit: 'what did she keep silent?', i.e. she spoke unspeakable things; quotation mark as in the source.

english: not unfaithful witnesses,
note: arbitrae: feminine, witnesses, agrees with Nox et Diana (line 51).

latin: Nox et Diana, quae silentium regis,
english: Night and Diana, who silence rule,
note: regis: second person, 'you who rule'.

english: when secret are performed rites,
note: arcana agrees with sacra.

latin: nunc, nunc adeste, nunc in hostilis domos
english: now, now be present, now against hostile houses
note: hostilis = hostiles, agreeing with domos.

english: your anger and divine power turn.
note: your supplied.

english: While in fearsome lie hidden woods the wild beasts,
note: formidulosis agrees with silvis.

english: with sweet slumber languid,
the old man, at which all may laugh, the adulterer,
note: quod omnes rideant: subjunctive, 'something for everyone to laugh at'; senem ... adulterum: Varus (line 73).

english: may they bark at, the Suburan bitches,
note: latrent: subjunctive (wish); canes: feminine, bitches of the Subura, the city's low district.

english: smeared all over with nard, such as nothing more perfect
note: quale: such an ointment as; perunctum agrees with senem (line 57).

english: my hands could have worked.
note: laborarint: perfect subjunctive (potential).

latin: quid accidit? cur dira barbarae minus
english: What has happened? Why dread the barbarian less
note: dira agrees with venena (line 62); barbarae agrees with Medeae (line 62).

english: poisons of Medea have power,
with which the proud she fled, avenged, rival,
